page.overview:
Who is Magna Mater?

Magna Mater is referenced as Cybele in the H. P. Lovecraft story "The Rats in the Walls".

The Miskatonic University Library Association Monograph supplement The Pastores identifies the Magna Mater as an avatar of Shub-Niggurath, held in worship in medieval France by an extensive cult of powerful humans and other supernatural entities.

Magna Mater is a Latin phrase meaning 'Great Mother' and was used historically as a title in Ancient Rome for both Cybele, a middle eastern cult with transvestite and eunuch priests and ecstatic public rituals and processions involving ritual slashing and blood spilling, and more generally in ancient syncretic religious beliefs as being the female principle in its highest and most powerful form, that of the giver of life, who impliedly could also take it away. In this sense it is cognate with the "Earth Monster" from South American ancient religion or the Amazonian Yacumama. More simply, a humanoid personification of Mother Nature as both the mother of us all, and the soil to which we will return.
